name: Question 5
problem:
A tank initially holds $600\,\text{gal}$ of a brine (salt-water) solution containing $18\,\text{lb}$ of salt.
A brine solution containing $0.02\,\text{lb}$ of salt per gallon flows into the tank at a rate of $15\,\text{gal/min},$ while the completely mixed brine leaves the tank at a rate of $20\,\text{gal/min}.$ Which differential equation best describes the amount of salt $Q,$ in pounds, in the tank $t$ minutes after the inflow begins?
worked_solution:
Since $Q$ is the amount of salt in the tank at time $t,$ the derivative 

$$
\frac{dQ}{dt}
$$

describes how this amount changes with respect to time $t,$ in minutes. This is equal to the rate at which salt enters the tank minus the rate at which salt leaves the tank.

$$
\frac{dQ}{dt}={Q}_{\text{in}}^{′}-{Q}_{\text{out}}^{′}
$$

Note that the units of $\frac{dQ}{dt},{Q}_{\text{in}}^{′}$ and ${Q}_{\text{out}}^{′}$ are $\text{lb}/\text{min}.$ Now, let's compute the required rates of change in steps.

**Step 1**: Calculating the rate at which salt enters the tank.

The inflowing brine has concentration $0.02\,\text{lb/gal}$ and flows into the tank at a rate of $15\,\text{gal}/\text{min}.$ So, the rate at which the *salt* enters the tank is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{Q}_{\text{in}}^{′} & =(0.02\,\frac{\text{lb}}{\text{gal}})\cdot (15\,\frac{\text{gal}}{\text{min}}) \\  & =(0.02\,\frac{\text{lb}}{\cancel{\text{gal}}})\cdot (15\,\frac{\cancel{\text{gal}}}{\text{min}}) \\  & =0.3\,\frac{\text{lb}}{\text{min}} \\  & =\frac{3}{10}\,\frac{\text{lb}}{\text{min}}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Calculating the rate at which salt exits the tank.

Now, to find the rate at which salt leaves the tank, we must first determine the volume of brine in the tank at time $t.$

- The tank initially contains $600\,\text{gal}$ of brine.

- Brine enters the tank at a rate of $15\,\text{gal/min}.$ So, after $t$ minutes, $15t\,\text{gal}$ have entered the tank.

- The completely mixed brine leaves the tank at a rate of $20\,\text{gal/min}.$ So, after $t$ minutes, $20t\,\text{gal}$ have left the tank.

As a result, the volume of brine in the tank after $t$ minutes is 

$$
600+15t-20t=(600-5t)\,\text{gal}.
$$

Since $Q$ is the mass of salt in the tank, the *concentration* of the brine at time $t$ is

$$
\frac{Q}{600-5t}\,\frac{\text{lb}}{\text{gal}}.
$$

Therefore, as the completely mixed brine leaves at a rate of $20\,\text{gal/min},$ *salt* leaves at a rate of

$$
\begin{aligned}{Q}_{\text{out}}^{′} & =(20\,\frac{\text{gal}}{\text{min}})\cdot (\frac{Q}{600-5t}\,\frac{\text{lb}}{\text{gal}}) \\  & =(20\,\frac{\cancel{\text{gal}}}{\text{min}})\cdot (\frac{Q}{600-5t}\,\frac{\text{lb}}{\cancel{\text{gal}}}) \\  & =\frac{20Q}{600-5t}\,\frac{\text{lb}}{\text{min}} \\  & =\frac{4Q}{120-t}\,\frac{\text{lb}}{\text{min}}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Calculate the overall rate of change.

Finally, the rate of change equals the rate of entry minus the rate of exit: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dQ}{dt} & ={Q}_{\text{in}}^{′}-{Q}_{\text{out}}^{′} \\  & =\frac{3}{10}-\frac{4Q}{120-t}\end{aligned}
$$

which finally gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dQ}{dt}+\frac{4}{120-t}Q=\frac{3}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

A tank initially holds 600gal of a brine (salt-water) solution containing 18lb of salt. A brine solution containing 0.02lb of salt per gallon flows into the tank at a rate of 15gal/min, while the completely mixed brine leaves the tank at a rate of 20gal/min. Which differential equation best describes the amount of salt Q, in pounds, in the tank t minutes after the inflow begins?

a
dQdt+4120−tQ=310
b
dQdt−4120−tQ=310
c
dQdt−3120−tQ=310
d
dQdt+1120−tQ=310
e
dQdt+3120−tQ=310
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since Q is the amount of salt in the tank at time t, the derivative dQdt describes how this amount changes with respect to time t, in minutes. This is equal to the rate at which salt enters the tank minus the rate at which salt leaves the tank.

dQdt=Qin′−Qout′

Note that the units of dQdt,Qin′ and Qout′ are lb/min. Now, let's compute the required rates of change in steps.

Step 1: Calculating the rate at which salt enters the tank.

The inflowing brine has concentration 0.02lb/gal and flows into the tank at a rate of 15gal/min. So, the rate at which the salt enters the tank is

Qin′=(0.02lbgal)⋅(15galmin)=(0.02lbgal)⋅(15galmin)=0.3lbmin=310lbmin.

Step 2: Calculating the rate at which salt exits the tank.

Now, to find the rate at which salt leaves the tank, we must first determine the volume of brine in the tank at time t.

  • The tank initially contains 600gal of brine.

  • Brine enters the tank at a rate of 15gal/min. So, after t minutes, 15tgal have entered the tank.

  • The completely mixed brine leaves the tank at a rate of 20gal/min. So, after t minutes, 20tgal have left the tank.

As a result, the volume of brine in the tank after t minutes is 600+15t−20t=(600−5t)gal.

Since Q is the mass of salt in the tank, the concentration of the brine at time t is Q600−5tlbgal.

Therefore, as the completely mixed brine leaves at a rate of 20gal/min, salt leaves at a rate of Qout′=(20galmin)⋅(Q600−5tlbgal)=(20galmin)⋅(Q600−5tlbgal)=20Q600−5tlbmin=4Q120−tlbmin.

Step 3: Calculate the overall rate of change.

Finally, the rate of change equals the rate of entry minus the rate of exit:

dQdt=Qin′−Qout′=310−4Q120−t which finally gives

dQdt+4120−tQ=310.
